Convert MSCZ to MP3 in the browser

What this does

MSCZ is MuseScore's compressed score format — notation, layout and instrument data, with no audio in it. Converting it to MP3 means rendering the score through a soundfont so you get a playable file. This page opens the converter with MP3 already selected; the rendering happens in your browser and the score is never uploaded.

Open the converter with the format selected

How to convert

  1. Choose your .mscz or .mscx file.
  2. Output format is already set to MP3 — press Convert.
  3. Download the rendered file when the progress bar finishes.

What you get

MP3 is audio and has no layout or page breaks. The sound comes from FluidR3Mono_GM.sf3 (General MIDI), so these are general GM sounds, not the sample library in your DAW. Tempo, dynamics and instruments are rendered as written in the score. Export PDF if you need the layout.

FAQ

Does the MP3 keep the score's layout?

No. MP3 is audio only — layout, page breaks and engraving are not part of the file. Export PDF if you need the printed score.

Can I convert an .mscx file the same way?

Yes. .mscx is the uncompressed MuseScore format; drop it in the same box and choose MP3.

Is my file uploaded to a server?

No. The conversion runs in your browser with WebMScore (WebAssembly); only the soundfont and the page assets are downloaded.
